interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Eva has outdone herself this year to make sure the Games are an event to remember. Perform well, and you'll win the right to light the ceremonial torches in the Tower. Along with a year's worth of bragging rights, as Eva would like me to remind you."

"There is a new challenge for you to overcome: Rushdown. Here's what you need to know." Zavala hands you a missive that reads:

RUSHDOWN
• Guardians are tasked with defeating 5 powerful combatants before the timer runs out.
• Each combatant defeated will increase the difficulty of combat.
• Guardians earn points by progressing quickly to reach higher score thresholds.
• Each day, there is a new combination of 5 powerful combatants to overcome.

Never a dull moment for the Vanguard. While Zavala orchestrates regular operations across the system and directs the fight to keep our hold on the Moon, he trusts you and Ikora to tackle the Vex crisis head-on.

headerDisplayProperties.description: Speak with Zavala about the emerging Vex crisis on the Moon.
headerDisplayProperties.name: The Vex Offensive

interactions.flavorLineOne:
The perpetually concerned look on Zavala's face lifts briefly as you approach.

"I see that your recent victories haven't dulled your edge. You're still pushing yourself to get better every day—an example I hope our New Lights follow."

"It's easy lose ourselves in the heady cosmic concerns that threaten the City, but in the heat of battle, a Guardian is only as good as their training."

He nods appreciatively at your battle-worn armor. "And I rest easy knowing that nobody trains harder than you."

Zavala looks exhausted, but alert. He hails you warmly as you approach.

"It's important that everyone in the Tower sees you training so fiercely. Your legend now exceeds even my own. Everyone looks up to you - both civilians and Lightbearers alike."

"You may not be a member of the Vanguard, but you set the tone for the Tower. Your work in the field is the realization of all of our efforts, right down to the sweeper bots."

"Thank you for taking your role, and our safety, as seriously as you do."

Zavala is amazed by your continuing ability to do the impossible. On behalf of the City, he thanks you for saving Saint-14. He also asks that you help Saint-14 adjust to his new life in the Tower however you can. He expects his return to the City will be a little overwhelming.

headerDisplayProperties.description: Commander Zavala has heard of your success in saving Saint-14 from the Infinite Forest and wishes to thank you. Visit him in the Tower Courtyard.
headerDisplayProperties.name: Zavala

interactions.flavorLineOne: Zavala is grateful that you defeated Kridis, but he now has other concerns. He believes that any compromise regarding the Darkness will only lead to disaster. Now that Eramis and her council are defeated, Guardians must no longer wield the Darkness. He hopes you'll respect this decision and help defend it. The people of the Last City need you now more than ever.

Now that Eramis is defeated, the Vanguard hopes to reclaim Europa for humanity. Zavala asks your help in destabilizing what remains of House Salvation. He informs you that Variks will help guide you through your first mission: sabotaging a Fallen weapons factory on Europa.

Return to Variks on Europa for more details.

"Congratulations on your performance in this year's Guardian Games. You should be proud of your accomplishments, regardless of the outcome. It's time to honor all of our classes and celebrate their achievements. Visit the podium to see the results of this year's competition." —Commander Zavala
Zavala's expression is unreadable as he accepts the cookies, but he nods in recognition of the thoughtful gift.

No need to waver, Guardian. The Vanguard stands behind you every step of the way.

The Light is our strength. The Darkness will never take that from us. 

Fight on.

"Riskrunner suits you, Guardian. I had planned to add it to the Tower's vault, but based on your performance, I think the only suitable place for it is in your hands.

"Weapons like this are the backbone of our arsenal. As you continue your journey, you would be wise to seek out other remarkable assets.

"Only by combining our Light with the most powerful of armaments can we hope to succeed against the enemies of humanity. Remember that, Guardian."
Zavala has called us to answer for our actions, but he seems reluctant to restrict your off-world activities.

"Exemplary work, Guardian. Strikes are an important component in our defense of humanity. As of now, I'm approving you for our full range of strike protocols; we're always in need of more fireteams ready to take the fight to the enemy's door."

Zavala holds one hand against the other palm.

"Now it's time for you to commemorate your success. You're ready for the next Guardian Rank. The ceremony starts at the tree behind you."

Zavala smiles.

"Don't delay."

Zavala's gaze is weighty, a mixture of pride, worry, and hope.

"Congratulations on reaching the second Guardian Rank. If you ever lack clarity on what to do next, the Ranks offer constructive guidance."

"There are two important tasks ahead of you. First, the superconducter. Completed analysis tells us it's exactly what we hoped for. We believe it can be used to reconstruct a powerful Arc weapon; a salvaged piece of Golden Age technology."

"Ikora Rey led the research efforts; she'll brief you on the specifics."

"We stand alongside more friends than ever before." The Humans of Neomuna are just as much included in that as those of the Last City. They have stood fast on the front lines of this conflict, and because of them, the Last City has been saved from more violence at its doorstep.

It isn't everything, but that thin line has made a huge difference.

"Now, I look up and see the hope we've built for ourselves." There is a gentle awe in the way Zavala regards the sky: the fleets of ships, the symbols of allies of the Last City. The Vanguard is no longer one last bastion against the Witness, but one of many.

Even without the Traveler, we are not alone.

And we'll need all the allies we can get. This war is far from over. Ikora has been in contact with Osiris regarding the mysteries yet unsolved. Visit her to learn more.

interactions.flavorLineOne: You've been at Gambit for a while now. You've met the enemies of Humanity head-on and made them pay. The Drifter has rewarded you handsomely for the Motes of Dark you've collected. Now it's time to see the culmination of your partnership with the Drifter.
Drifter's smile never falters as he accepts the delicious chocolate treats.
"Hey, I see you. I know what you're about. Come to the Tower. A Guardian like you should get to know a fella like me. The benefits would be… mutual." —The Drifter

Drifter stands up straight and slides something quickly out of view behind his back.

"Well, well, what can I do for—oh, it's you, hero. That's a mighty fine mask you got on there. Almost fooled 'ol Drifter. 'Cept for the, uh, tape you got hanging there."

You inquire about the missing grab bags, but he shakes his head.

"That's the kind of trouble you'll never find me lookin' for. Last thing I want is to end up as Eva's next Dawning cookie!"

He mentions hearing rumors about Exo boot prints leading out of the storage room where Eva keeps her extra grab bags.

He shudders. "But if Eva asks, you didn't hear that from me."

headerDisplayProperties.name: The Mystery of the Missing Bags

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Drifter flashes a crooked smile as you walk up. "Nice work, hotshot," he says. "You're almost ready to go grab that gun."

"According to those blueprints, the one thing the Fallen haven't worked out yet is how to stabilize the Stasis energy. So I whipped up a prototype of my own." He winks. "This should help you get the gun firing."

Return to Europa and complete the "Stealing Stasis" mission.

"Like I said, kid; when Drifter wins, you win. Don't ever say I didn't do anything for you.

"Whenever you feel like making some more cheddar, you come on back. Don't be shy about it; Gambit's always here, and Drifter never forgets his friends."
You found a component part of some kind of weapon at Callum's grave. It must be what he stole from the Drifter. He'd probably like it back.
You've defeated a particularly powerful Primeval in Gambit and taken its heart. Drifter might find it valuable. Take it to him.
Drifter is impressed. He admires the gun and asks you to bring it through Gambit sometime. This weapon could really shake things up.

"Hey, hero." Drifter has a familiar insouciance as he greets you.

"Got something here for you. Some kind of challenge. Yeah, I know you're up for anything. Whaddaya think: your greatest foes, given renewed strength? Sound good?"

The bravado falls away a little. Drifter's look is briefly sympathetic.

"It's only gonna get worse," he reminds you. "Whatever the Nine put in front of their Weapon. You can kill anything, Guardian. Time to prove it."

He's back to a grin inside of a moment.

"And hey, you'll get a good prize out of it! That's what I'm talking about."
Visit the Drifter in the Annex.

"I knew you'd be back before too long. Old Drifter presents opportunities that are too good to pass up…

"Here's the game, kid; it's called Gambit, a friendly competition between Guardians with the Darkness sandwiched in the middle. Every time you play, I get some cheese, and I kick some of that back to my friend, you dig?

"And when I say friend, I mean you. We're in this together, you see? When you win, Drifter wins, and when Drifter wins, you win. Heck of a scheme if I say so myself.

"So get out there and give it a spin, yeah?"

The Drifter examines the blueprints you found. Turns out that the Fallen are using Praksis's armor tech to create a weapon capable of channeling Stasis energy. Eramis had plans to distribute this weaponry to Fallen all across the system, expanding the capabilities of her army.

Drifter likes the idea so much that he immediately cooks up a plan to steal the prototype from the Fallen. He thinks Spider's associates might be able to offer some insider information too. While he looks over the blueprints and calls in a favor, he asks you to go to Europa and gather more intel on the prototype.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"The Loom requires material input to function; strands of basic matter that can be repurposed as needed," Ada explains.

"I've used the BrayTech schematics to create smaller devices called Threaders—with these, you can convert Glimmer into the Synthcord that the Loom needs. We should verify the Threaders are functioning before anything else…"

Purchase an Armor Synthesis bounty from Ada.

"I don't think there's much else for me to review with you. Please keep utilizing the Loom so I can compile more data—who knows where it will lead. And thank you again, Guardian."

She turns back to her workstation but stops abruptly, turning her attention back to you.

"What is it that old saying? The ball is in your court now?"

She tilts her head.

"I'm not really sure what that means—but good luck, friend."

Ada looks up from her work as you approach.

"I've been doing some experiments with the Sieve. Customized reinforcements for our veteran Guardians."

She gestures to some neatly stacked boxes, which light the room with an enticing yellow glow. 

"I discovered a method to reproduce some of our most effective armor. It worked wonderfully but proved too expensive for mass production."

"It would be a waste to let the prototypes go unused, so the Vanguard authorized me to distribute them." She hands you a small pile of requisition orders.

"Just remember—I only have so many to hand out. Once you've made your selections, let me know, and I'll pull them out of storage for you."
Ada is awestruck at what she has accomplished with the Loom, and relieved to have a new beginning for the Armory. She thanks you for your help and expresses excitement about the future.
Ada-1 examines the gift skeptically. Eventually, she looks up and thanks you, but she still seems perplexed by the exchange.

"Here it is—the first printing," Ada says tenuously.

"This is Synthweave, a programmable matter more sophisticated than I've ever seen, significantly more advanced than Glimmer."

She hands you a sample of the Loom's output.

"Do the honors of trying it out. It should be able to replicate the physical appearance of some of your armor, though not the material or energy properties."

Use Synthweave to create an ornament from your collection of Legendary armor.

Ada tells you that the Black Armory Forges have been lost. In their absence, she is working on a new project; some unfinished research she unearthed in the BrayTech archives on Europa.

She says she needs help retrieving the last remaining research data from Europa's surface, as it's not accessible via the network.

Travel to the BrayTech facility on Europa and recover the data.

"Good," Ada says as she types feverishly on her workstation.

"I used the data you streamed from Europa to make some final adjustments to the device.

"The original plans from Clovis are out of reach — whatever he wanted to make from this, it requires theoretical alloys that don't exist. Given what we know about him now, maybe it's best if that vision never comes to fruition…

"In any case, I was able to use some concepts from the original Forge designs to finish the prototype. It's my own design now.

She steps back from the workstation.

"The processing unit is the final piece. You retrieved it, it's only fair that you get to close this out."

Interact with the Loom prototype to connect the processing unit.

Ada admires your newly minted Synthweave as you approach.

"I must admit, it was a little unnerving to watch someone else operate the Loom. I've put quite a lot of effort into creating this and… I'm feeling a bit protective."

She clears her throat and fixes her posture.

"That being said, it clearly worked as intended. I've gathered data from your production job—with enough information, I may be able to amend this technology toward some other purpose in the future."

"To that end, let's start another production run."

 Acquire Glimmer in order to purchase another Armor Synthesis bounty from Ada-1.

Ada's mechanical fingers clack away at a glass touchscreen. "Initial readouts look promising—power levels are stable and the operating system hasn't hit any assertions."

She says the words carefully and meticulously, like they don't fit well around her voice yet.

"As far as I can tell, the Loom is ready for production. Let me give it a test run and see what we get, and if it passes quality checks, I'll explain the process."

interactions.flavorLineOne: Devrim is polite as always in his gratitude and waits for you to depart before returning his attention to the window.

"I met Cayde enough times to know a thing or two about his codenames for things. Cosmonaut Club…"

Devrim scratches his beard and stares out the window of the steeple.

"I'd bet the pot he's referring to the Cosmodrome. Must have been spooked by something and decided to relocate the package there."

"You're probably best off checking the interior of the Cosmodrome wall; that's the only place he could reliably hide something from the Fallen in Old Russia."

"Good luck, Guardian. Don't forget a coat. It gets a bit nippy in Siberia this time of year."

"Ah, welcome to my cozy hideaway, Guardian."

"Ikora said you'd be coming, told me what's what. Sounds like you're looking for a weapon frame. It was one of Cayde's old treasures, recovered during a Vanguard operation."

"I'm happy to help, but there's a bit of a snag. The former Hunter Vanguard was notorious for hiding his goodies behind elaborate puzzles. In this case, he divided the map containing the frame's location, and squirrelled the map components away."

Devrim pauses and shakes his head. "Unfortunately, that was a long time ago, and the Fallen have stolen the fragments of Cayde's map. Hard to finish the jigsaw without all the pieces, eh?"

"You raid some Fallen Lost Sectors, I bet you'll find what you need. Cheers, and good luck."

Devrim nods approvingly at your scratched and spattered armor.

"I've been watching you battle back Maya's forces. Impressive stuff. With a sustained effort like that, we may even be able to resettle the Plaguelands someday."

His optimistic tone becomes tempered by years of war fatigue.

"But I still don't think we've gotten to the bottom of Maya's ambitions in the region. Keep working with Caiatl's Psions to learn what her endgame is with all this Golden Age tech."

The sniper gives you a jaunty salute. "Keep up the good work, Guardian."

Devrim waves you over with a fire in his eyes.

"Maya's attack on the Tower started a new gold rush across Sol. She's losing control of her collective and needs the latent power from Golden Age tech to maintain it."

Devrim gives your loadout a quick up-and-down, nodding in approval.

"We need to beat her forces to that tech and reclaim lost territories while you're there. We'll be inserting you into some former quarantine zones, so be ready for anything."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Maya and Chioma are pleased with the data you've managed to glean from the Vex thus far.

While all they need for their work is information on the Conductor's whereabouts, that's not all they've managed to collect. They offer you their preliminary research on VexNet matter-conversion formulae with gratitude, in the hopes you'll find something valuable within it.

You can now attune to armor from "The Desert Perpetual." Complete additional steps to unlock attunement for more gear.

Maya and Chioma are pleased with the data you've managed to glean from the Vex thus far.

While all they need for their work is information on the Conductor's whereabouts, that's not all they've managed to collect. They offer you their preliminary research on VexNet matter-conversion formulae with gratitude, in the hopes you'll find something valuable within it.

You can now attune to armor from "The Desert Perpetual." Complete additional steps to unlock attunement for more gear.

The Simulant Ansible presses at the border of Unknown Space and the Vex Network, connecting the threads of simulated worlds beyond number. 227.50 Chioma Esi, herself a simulation of the Vex and a longtime explorer of the Network, speaks to you through its towering figure.

"Maya and I are at different points within the Net. With you, we make three."

"Three points of triangulation: the first step towards a map," Maya adds. "The Vex use their network for simulations, billions of them layered one atop the other. At points of similarity, they converge."

Chioma and Maya can use the nature of the Ansible to call forth a series of anchors with which you may connect the web of Vex simulations.

With the determination of one committed to the impossible, Chioma tells you: "We can begin to chart the VexNet itself."

The Simulant Ansible crackles to life once more, projecting voices from the other end of the Vex Network.

"We've charted paths within the Network, learned more about the Vex, and… Maya and I have found our way back to each other," 227.50 Chioma says. She adds, "All thanks to you."

227.87 Maya, now at Chioma's side, says, "Our work continues. We must rally the other exploratory teams, and we must stop the Conductor before she kills again. She may not be me, but I recognize myself in her. I owe it to Chioma to stop her. I owe it to myself."

"So, you're being self-serving," Chioma says, not without a fond twist of humor.

"It's part of my baseline." Maya's voice is wry. "We may as well use it."

Maya and Chioma will continue their work within the VexNet with the help of your map and wish you the best in your battles against the Vex outside it.

The ansible clicks and crackles before giving way to Maya and Chioma's voices, arriving from the simulation they've dubbed Green Moon Rho.

"The Conductor is out there somewhere. Her Echo is failing, and I am absolutely sure she's looking for some new power to compensate." Maya's voice is grim. She knows her other self better than anyone.

"We think we can find her. Or at least, narrow down the possibility of where in the VexNet she's working," Chioma says, determined. "You helped us find our way to each other—with a small tweak to our methods, I believe we can find her."

She adds with an audible smile for Maya, "I missed my research assistant."

Maya and Chioma sign off, ready for the work ahead. It's time to return to the anchors you've already placed and draw a path on your map.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Banshee spins a Wolfpack Round on his workbench, then stops it with his palm. "Perfectly balanced," he muses. "Not surprised. Crux really knew how to put these things together."

He looks up at you. "I wouldn't have thought forging a new Gjallarhorn was possible, but it seems that every day, the impossible gets a little closer."

He looks over at the vaults a few meters away, now brimming with the weapon stashes of countless Guardians. "We lost a lot in the Red War. The Fallen probably tucked what tech they could carry somewhere in the Cosmodrome. Check the old scav hangouts. Maybe Exodus Garden."

Banshee appears lost in thought for a moment. "Y'know, part of wielding the Gjallarhorn is honoring those who didn't make it. Parts should come from the armor of those we've lost… yeah. And we've lost a lot lately…"

He digs around under his table for a moment, then comes up with a battered trigger mechanism.

"I pieced this together a long time ago so I wouldn't forget some friends I had," he says, then looks down. "Didn't work. Maybe it's time to let go of the past, but still honor it."

He raps the tables with his metal knuckles. "Let's make this weapon one to remember."
"Job well done. This dragon's ready to roar." —Banshee-44
The Gunsmith has a delivery for you: an experimental prototype weapon from Omolon foundry.
"Good job. Veist knows what they're about. But so do you." —Banshee-44

Banshee-44 takes the Grenade Launcher from you and applies the catalyst.

"I had to do some real research into Hive stuff to figure out how to get it just right," he says.

"Saw some old names," he mutters. "Stirred up some old memories."

Work complete, he hands the weapon back to you with a wink.

"If you use that thing on Crota, tell him Banshee sent you."

"Looks like it worked," Banshee comments upon your return.

"Arcology's scientists were good, but they didn't have Guardians. Bet they never counted on channeling Arc Light through this thing."

He gives the weapon a final inspection, seemingly lost in thought.

"Heard about an old power source Sloane was carting around Titan for a time. Maybe this gun was meant to go with it."

Banshee shrugs as he hands the Centrifuse back to you.

"Guess we'll never know. Another memory, lost beneath the waves."

Banshee-44 takes your Delicate Tomb and, after a few moments, installs and calibrates the catalyst.

"That should do it," he says, but his mechanical brow furrows. 

"Touching that weapon again… I don't know why, but I don't feel good about making it stronger." He hands you the gun, but as you take it, he holds his grip for a moment and looks into your eyes.

"I know you can handle anything, Guardian," he says, "but some things might be better forgotten."

He releases the gun and goes back to his business.

Banshee stares silently at the weapon you place before him.

"Where did you…" he begins, but then stops. Carefully, he takes the incomplete weapon in his hands.

He tests its weight, its sights, considers the brutal efficiency of its design. "You've never brought me a piece like this before," he murmurs. "I'd remember."

Finally, he turns to you. "I can fix this," he says. "It won't be exactly how it was… I'll have to improvise. I don't know the make of any of these parts. I'm not even sure what kind of metal…"

He trails off again, then takes the weapon into the back of his shop.

"It'll shoot," he says when he reappears. "Thing'll kick like a warthog, but it'll shoot."

He hands you the sidearm with reverence. "A gun like that could make somebody a hero."

He chuckles. "Of course, it wouldn't hurt to be a hero to begin with."

Banshee holds a slug shotgun in his hand, intricately ornamented and gleaming with polished metal. He rotates it, testing the weight distribution, then quickly spins it by the lever. A shell ejects as it lands back in his hands, pointed at you.

"Same as you ever were, old friend."

He lowers the barrel and inspects the weapon.

"This weapon was in Holliday's family a long time. Helped her make it to this city…"

"Look out for your friends, Guardian. This shotgun will help you do just that."

Banshee-44 shivers as he holds the calibrated catalyst.

"There was some gun I was supposed to keep this away from," he says. "Something cold and dark. Can't really remember, though."

"Now that it's fully calibrated, maybe you could hold onto it to keep it safe."

His face brightens. "It might fit that Sidearm you've got there, in fact!"

Banshee-44 tosses you the catalyst, thanks you for your help, and goes back to polishing his weapons.

The gears turn in Banshee's head. Distant connections solidify into recognition.

"Right, let's see what you learned in the Throne World."

Banshee tinkers away at the workbench behind him, slowly turning with a completed weapon.

"Sweet, now back to business."

You approach Banshee's work table with the Anomalous Weapon Part in your hand. Banshee reaches across and snatches it from you before you can say a word.

"Would you look at that," he marvels, inspecting the part. "There's only one weapon I've ever seen that matches this make. It's not the kind of piece you'd forget. Give me a minute, and I'll tune it up for you."

He disappears with the piece for a moment, then reappears, chuckling to himself. "This much power in a sidearm… I can hardly tell if this is the world's biggest pistol or the world's smallest rifle."

"Fine tune this in the field and you'll be legendary," he says with a wink. "Go get 'em, Guardian."
"I remembered where the name Arbalest came from… or at least I had remembered. Hmm, well take 'er for a spin. Maybe that'll jog my memory."
"This should help you get that extra edge I was talkin' about," Banshee says. "Not that you need it."
"I remembered where the name Arbalest came from… or at least, I had remembered. Hmm, well take 'er for a spin. Maybe that'll jog my memory."

Banshee-44 briefly looks up from his work. "Zahn's always been a pain. Glad someone put him in his place."

"Sounds like you made an impression on Ikora. She asked me to find a Solar weapon for you." The weapon that he hands you looks untouched, fresh from the armory. "This can Scorch, just like you. Should play well with your armor and abilities."

When you don't immediately leave, Banshee speaks up once more. "Not often that Ikora puts in a request like this. If you want to keep learning, go back to her. I think she'll make time for you."

Check back with Ikora to continue learning about your Light, including other Aspects, abilities, Fragments, and keywords.

Banshee-44 seems to be expecting you. "So you're the one who blew up that old Servitor? Good riddance, that thing's better off as scrap."

"Got something for you. Ikora said you needed an Arc weapon." The weapon that he hands you looks untouched, fresh from the armory. "This can jolt, just like you. Should play well with your armor and abilities."

Banshee goes back to his work, but not without a parting word. "Bit of advice, Guardian. Get used to seeing Ikora if you want to keep learning." 

Check back with Ikora to continue learning about your Light, including learning about other Aspects, Fragments, abilities, and keywords.

Banshee-44 gives you a curious look. "Never understood anything Ikora said about the Void. But I know weapons, and she asked me to find one for you."

The weapon that he hands you looks untouched, fresh from the armory. "Let's say you debuff a target with Void. Drop them with this, and you'll get a Void barrier for protection. Should work well with your armor too."

He lapses into a thoughtful silence before speaking up again. "You're not bad at this, Guardian. But nobody knows everything. If you want to get better, ask Ikora to keep teaching you."

Check back with Ikora to continue learning about your Light, including other Aspects, Fragments, abilities, and keywords.

"Huh, look at that," Banshee says with an approving nod. "Linear modulator's looking good, thermal caster is intact, joints to the intake valves are nice and solid. Heck, this looks like as good a job as I'd do."

Banshee stares down at the catalyst, eyes slowly narrowing. "Wait, did I do this? Somebody did." He looks around, furtively, then slides you the catalyst.

"I don't know where I got this, but I think it'll work in your gun," Banshee says without any recognition in his eyes. "Here, take it."

"Never liked the Moon. Too many memories. Too many lost friends. Hate to see you end up the same… And I know you've walked where most wouldn't dare, but there's always lessons to learn, Guardian. Even some you think you already know."

Heed Banshee's words. Do as he asks, and earn an Exotic weapon catalyst for the Eriana's Vow Hand Cannon.

"That's all the energy this thing needs," nods Banshee-44 as he hands you the completed catalyst. "Let me tell you, I think there's something funny about this bow. It messes with my internal chronometer."

"It feels like that thing was meant for your hands. Like it always belonged there."

"Nice work, Guardian." Banshee-44 looks up from his workbench. He hands you the repaired catalyst. 

"All that Cabal tech you seized worked like a dream. It's fully operational, and ready for the field."

"Good luck out there. Not that you need it," he quips.

Banshee-44 takes the Verglas Curve from you and applies the catalyst.

"It's not as complex as the system a compound bow has," he explains as he restrings the weapon, "but it should give you a little extra kick."

He finishes, then lets his hands linger for a moment on the dark wood.

"There's something honest about a weapon built like this," he says. 

"Take good care of it."

"That catalyst polished up real nice," Banshee says. 

He hands it back to you and asks, "Who did the work?"

Ghost starts to answer, but Banshee's attention wanders to work on other weapons.

"See you around," he says.
"This should give you an edge in the field," Banshee says. "Happy to help."

"Looks like some things can come back even better than they were before," Banshee-44 says as he processes your data and feeds the results into the Duality.

"Wish it could be that easy for all of us."

"This thing is givin' me flashes left and right. But they're scrambled. Something about a bunker hidden away among the ice. Must be Europa. Gotta ask you to help one more time. We're close, I can feel it."
Banshee-44 blinks and stares at the gift, then takes it before you can question him.

"Arbalest… can't remember what this was named after. Either way, it's a handy weapon. You know what would help tune it just right? Getting some data from inside the Traveler's Pale Heart. You up for it?"
"Arbalest… can't remember what this was named after. Either way, it's a handy weapon. You know what would help tune it just right? Getting some data from Neomuna. You up for it? "
Banshee thinks he can help boost your weapon's performance, but he needs you to do some work in the field first.

Banshee is distant, taking far too long to notice your presence.

"Hm? Schematic? Yeah. Calibrate. Throne World."

"A Holliday family schematic…"

Banshee's eyes shimmer.

"Holding this reminds me of those harebrained schematics Amanda used to create."

"I'll need to see how it performs in extreme temperatures. Europa might be a good spot to generate some data below freezing points. How about it?"

"Didn't I ask Shaw to take care of this? Hmm, Holliday was right: 'delegate' might be his favorite word."

"Been trying to fix up an old family heirloom of Holliday's for a while now, something to remember her by. This'll help me calibrate the tooling. Only…"

Banshee wipes the grease from his forehead.

"Where did I put those charts? I'm going to need some time to crunch these numbers. Come back in a bit."

"Let's see," Banshee says, leaning against the counter. "I think I could give this weapon a boost for you. Something to help you out in the field."

He nods. "But first, I need to see how you handle it. Get me some data, and I'll see what I can do."
Complete activities to prove your mastery of Eriana's Vow and Banshee will reward you with an Exotic weapon catalyst.
"Some guns need to finish what they started long ago. You're just along for the ride." —Banshee-44

"Well… that did it. I can see a bit clearer now. The thing—the big Exo head… It's me. And I'm… it. Both of us, Clovis Bray. Well that's… certainly something.

"I don't feel like the old man. But it's coming into focus more each minute.

"I know now I used that Sword to repel a takeover by the Vex during the Golden Age. Looks like you've done somethin' similar. No need to hand it over; it's yours now.

"Thanks for protecting, well, me. I think I'll be makin' a trip over there at some point. Visit my giant self. Learn more about who I was.

"I've got questions, and it sounds like I've also got answers. Hopefully I've got nothing left to answer for."

"You know, once upon a time, we didn't put onboard AIs into our weapons." The grim Exo looks over the auto rifle. "Those were dark times. Things are much more interesting now." 

He sets to work, making minuscule adjustments to the auto rifle's frame. "Programs can do a lot, but sometimes you just need to get your hands in there…" 

The nanites apparently take his lead, because when he finally returns the weapon to you, the balance feels better, the weight adjusts in your hand to perfect levels as you hold it. Banshee's grin is wicked and joyful. "One last set of calibrations. Call it high-impact testing."

interactions.flavorLineOne: Banshee-44 wants to speak with you about the history of the Witherhoard.

"I've got a catalyst for that bow of yours," Banshee-44 says. "I think I've always had it, but I don't remember getting it."

"Charge the catalyst with energy and I'll work on it for you… but next time, can you just bring me a regular gun? Nothing that collapses timelines or whatever?"

"Bunch of Guardians storm the Deep Stone Crypt and next thing I know, I wake up in a daze sprawled out on the floor.

"Seems crazy to assume the two are connected, but then again, stranger things and all that, y'know?

"Now you walk in here and my insides go haywire all over again.

"Lotta weird images flashin' through my mind. Hard to make sense of 'em all. Vex… a blade… And a few dead Exos on Europa, unhappy with their lot in life, I imagine.

"Not sure what that's about. Maybe see about findin' 'em? Help me make sense of all this. I'll be waitin'."

—Banshee-44

"Folks are saying Ada-1's back? Don't remember her leaving," Banshee grumbles. His eyes narrow, but he doesn't stop repairing the Auto Rifle on his desk.

"Come to think of it, I guess I didn't see her for a while… anyway, I hear she's asking Guardians for help. Got some new project in the works, something about programmable matter… and Europa? The Fallen too… Hard to keep the details straight, but I'm glad she's keeping busy."

The servos in his hand whirr quietly as he works on the weapon.

"Maybe pay her a visit? Whatever she's making, I'm sure it's worth your time. She's always been a special talent."

You overhear Banshee-44 talking to himself as you approach.

"Never saw a gun like that before," he says quietly. "Thing would go cold in your hands. Nothing good can come from a piece like that."

"Hey, Guardian," he says as he notices you. "Do me a favor: you ever find a Sidearm that runs cold, you be sure to keep this catalyst far away from it, y'hear?"

He holds up a damaged Sidearm catalyst.

"'Course, thing's busted pretty bad now. I'd need plenty of calibration data to get it up and running again."

"Get me some, would you?"
Banshee offers to help you improve your new Auto Rifle, Tommy's Matchbook.

"Hear me out," Banshee says as he slams part of a jumpship drive and a datapad on the counter. "Your gun uses a Lorentz focuser to channel energized particles, so does this old Echo-class jump drive. Before it blew up. Unrelated."

"If we mod your gun with these drive components, we'll be able to give it a lot more…" Banshee says before slamming his fist down on the counter. Then he just stares vacantly for a moment and asks, "What're you doing here? Oh, right. Hear me out," Banshee says. "Your gun uses a Lorentz focuser to…"

You take the jump drive parts and the datapad before Banshee goes through his plan all over again.

"This is a fine looking piece of Cabal scrap," Banshee-44 says, turning the catalyst over in his hands. 

"But it needs to be rebuilt before you can use it in the field."

"Lucky for you," he continues, "I got a plan. All we need is some Cabal tech to study…"

Banshee takes a look at your gun and nods his approval. "I like the look of this one," he says. "But I bet I can help you kick it up a notch."

He leans back and crosses his arms. "Let me know if you want my help."

"This came in for you. Tech is Fallen. Could ask, uh… Splicers—yeah."

Banshee looks proud and then flips the piece over. "Wait… no. Forgot about this."

Banshee pulls a pin from the frame of the catalyst. He holds it up to looks at it. It lights up and emits a tiny projection of Calus.

"Welcome to my little game of tribute," the projection says. "If you want your treasure, you'll have to pay in blood."

"You are a trespasser in my home, just as the Fallen trespass in your home. Rid your home of the trespassers, and my gift will be yours."

The projection finishes with booming laughter and shuts off.

"Huh," grunts Banshee.

"Eriana went to the Moon. Many did. None came back. Well… Eris did. But that wasn't 'til later. And she came back… different.

"My point's not about the loss though. Point is they went. Despite the odds. Despite the unknown.

"Eriana may be gone, but that gun means she's still with us. Still able to teach Guardians lessons worth learnin'."

Banshee-44 looks at your Delicate Tomb and whistles.

"Nice-lookin' weapon, Guardian," he says. He takes it from you and tests its weight. "Very—"

A strange look crosses the Exo's face. "Huh," he says quietly, "thought I heard something."

"Anyway," he says as he quickly hands the weapon back to you, "it's old construction, not anything I recognize, but I might know a way to tune it up."

He sends you back out into the field.
Head back to the Tower and speak to Banshee-44 about the broken blade.

Banshee-44 takes your Manticore and considers it carefully.

"Got some old parts," he says, deep in concentration. "I remember—what was it? It was a long time ago."

He shakes his head as if trying to shake a thought from his mind. The Exo hands the weapon back to you with a look of resolve.

"Won't be too hard to punch it up. No reason we have to settle for what's given."
Banshee-44 believes he can design a catalyst for the Exotic Shotgun Duality.

As you place the Verglas Curve in front of Banshee-44, a look of confusion crosses his face.

"Hey, look. I said I could improve your new weapon, but I didn't know it was…" he trails off as he picks up the bow and eyes it skeptically. 

"Is this made of… wood?"

He runs his metal fingers over the bowstring and delicate ferns of frost sprout from the tension. 

"Oh. Stasis," he grumbles. "I heard about Guardians using some kind of yarn power… well, at least I understand this." 

"Okay," he says with a shrug, "if you can shoot it, I can improve it. Any catalyst for this weapon would have been lost long ago, so we'll have to recreate one." 

He hands the bow back to you. "Take it to the field and let's figure out how it works."

Banshee examines the charred Centrifuse with a sharp eye.

"Impressive stuff," he mutters to himself before looking back to you.

"Cutting edge Golden Age tech. Some burnt out components, but… hmm…"

He crosses his arms in front of his chest and nods slowly to himself.

"Yeah. There's potential here. Need you to do some calibrating first, though."

"What are you doing?" Banshee-44 exclaims as you place the weapon before him. "You can't just take guns from the Hive and expect me to…"

He trails off as he picks up the weapon and turns it over in his hands. 

"Who's been working on this? Eris?" he wonders to himself. "She must have had Brya help."

He holds one of the dangling cards between his metal fingers and squints.

"These use Hive magic to keep the weapon intact, huh?" he says. "Smart. A little creepy, but smart."

Finally, he nods and hands the weapon back.

"You don't need to be a thanatonaut to see this thing has some deep ties to the other side. You want to earn its respect, you'll have to do a lot of killing, and not as much dying."

interactions.flavorLineOne: Saint-14 opens his arms to you when you arrive with his gift. He accepts the cookies, sets them aside, and then clasps your hand warmly. He wishes you a happy Dawning.

Saint-14 bows his head to you. "A fellow warrior of the Light. Come close, let me guide your path to the Lighthouse, my friend." Saint explains that to enter the Trials of Osiris, you must possess a Trials Passage. Your passage will track your round or match wins. Each passage offers a different experience.

Saint looks over a blank passage. "You want as many wins as possible, obviously…" he chuckles. He continues, saying that seven wins on a Lighthouse Passage grants access to the Lighthouse for extra rewards. "I await your ascension to the Lighthouse. Good luck."

You can reset your Trials Passage on the item in your Quests tab, or on the Trials of Osiris activity node.

You approach Saint-14; the crest of his helm brims with sunlight. "You are ready for a mighty tournament!" He straightens his stance and looks you over.

"You will not win the Trials of Osiris with only strength. Here, we test teamwork!" His voice rises, punctuating the final word. "You should fight with those you trust. If you fall, your friends must bring you back in the fight." 

Saint leans in, and he sounds more like his usual self. "Do not worry! Even defeat teaches lessons. If you lose, you can still test yourself against other Guardians on the way to the Lighthouse. Or start over and try again, until you are undefeated." You can almost hear the grin in his voice. "Fight hard, and you will be rewarded. But better rewards if you win, yes?"

As you approach Saint-14, you notice a suspiciously large number of well-fed pigeons have gathered around him, all cooing at top volume.

"Hello, noble guard! I suppose you're here about the noise complaints?" Saint asks. His voice is proud and booming as ever, but his gauntleted hands twist nervously.

You shake your head. He breaks instantly. "Ah, well, listen… My little friends looked so hungry. A holiday treat couldn't hurt. Do birds not also deserve to celebrate those they have lost? Eva always makes so many spare, I thought she would not notice any missing."

"Perhaps for the best for their digestion and my carpets, Eva's bags had no candy within. But the local ramen shop had a sack of corn to spare! Much better for their little pigeon bellies."

Saint turns to poke through his supplies and digs out the final surviving bag, only lightly pecked. "I have acted shamefully. I will apologize to Ms. Levante! Here, bring this back to her, my good and perceptive guard."

You stay silent, hoping Saint-14 doesn't recognize you under the mask. With an awkward salute, you leave him to clean up after his birds.

Saint-14 greets you with an approving nod. "How do you feel? Tired? Triumphant? Both?" 

Before you can answer, his laugh echoes through the Hangar. "I knew you would do well, Guardian. So I saved this for you." He extends a gleaming weapon to you; the Hangar's lights glitter off its surface.

"Remember, the more you win in Trials, the better! Stronger weapons will help. But the rest… that is up to you."

Saint-14 is overjoyed that you have chosen to take part in the Trials of Osiris. He tries to contain his excitement as he delivers his wonderfully rehearsed speech. Afterward, he nods and says, "I know you will give this everything, Guardian. You've never been one to hold back."

interactions.flavorLineOne: "I found one more gift for you to finish the festival strong."

"Guardian," Eva intones, face backlit with the flickering light of holiday candles. "Listen now to my tale of vengeance and woe!"

She waggles her outspread fingers, making the shadows around her dance. But her tone is serious.

"I arranged Mystery Grab Bags to give everyone an exciting and meaningful Festival of the Lost. And now some of them have gone missing! I suspect someone hungry, lurking around in a basement… if you catch my DRIFT."

"I see you're ready for the Festival with a very official mask of your own. In the spirit of the season, I'd appreciate if you found the culprit and gave them a good scare."

Eva leans in to whisper conspiratorially to you. "Don't tell the other Guardians, but if you help me out, you can keep one of the bags for yourself."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Eva smiles warmly as you approach. She already holds a small parcel in her hands, as though she had been anticipating your arrival.

"One of my favorite parts of the Dawning is that I get to see my favorite people every day," she says as she hands you the parcel.

"Thank you for taking the time to visit me. Now, go spread this good cheer with the rest of your friends!"

Eva accepts the cookies with a warm smile. "Happy Dawning to you," she says. "Things may be grim at times, but the world is full of things that remind us never to give up hope."

She laughs. "I'm talking about you, Guardian. Of course, the cookies help, too."
"A truly impressive showing! You've proved yourself to be one of the top Guardians of any class. I hope you'll wear this emblem with the pride it deserves." —Eva Levante
"A gift need not be material. Sometimes your presence, a little favor, or some advice is just as welcome. The Dawning is a time to care for one another." —Eva Levante
"What a bounty! I hope you didn't play too many tricks to earn these treats!" —Eva Levante

"Happy Solstice, Guardian."

Eva welcomes you to the celebration, smiling with deep warmth. 

"I am so pleased to see you here. There is always something special about Solstice, isn't there? We remember what has been, and we celebrate the life and hope of here and now, of the future yet to come with the people by our sides."

"I have asked Zavala to devise some exciting new challenges for you to overcome this year, Guardian. You'll have access to these during your Operations this Solstice. It is our hope that these will drive you to ever greater heights, and that you shine brightly for all to see."

"Welcome back, Guardian."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Death is part of a Cloud Strider's lot. Nimbus knows this, but that doesn't make Rohan's early exit any easier to accept. 

Still, he made every moment count; by destroying the Radial Mast, Rohan wrecked the Witness's plan for creating a link with the Veil.

But that doesn't mean the war is over. Calus is sure to retaliate—and it looks like his sights are set on the CloudArk. 

There's no time to mourn now. The best way to honor Rohan is to get Neomuna's defense systems up and running again.

You might check in with Osiris and Caiatl in the Hall of Heroes before jumping back into the fray. 

Complete the strike "HyperNet Current" in Neomuna.
"Been seeing a few more hopeful faces around lately. Knowing you're here to help really keeps morale up, you know? The people of Neomuna appreciate it, and so do I." —Nimbus

"Y'know, word in the CloudArk is, there's someone from Earth running around the city. Except they aren't a Warlord trying to take over, they're a Guardian here to help and kick butt. How about that, huh?" —Nimbus

Calus beat us to the Veil and secured it on behalf of the Witness. Luckily, its containment infrastructure should delay their efforts, at least for a little while. Based on Ghost's strange experience, it appears Calus intends to use a device called the Radial Mast to link the Veil with the Traveler.

Whatever the Witness wants, this can't be good. With Calus's forces focused on the Veil containment, Osiris wants us to hit Calus's fortress directly and take out this Radial Mast before it is moved closer to the Veil. Even despite Rohan's concerns.

Nimbus recommends you check in with Rohan and Osiris at the Hall of Heroes before moving on to mission "Downfall."

Nimbus takes the Vex compass and Seed of Silver Wings off your hands. They don't mention Osiris insisting they stay behind, though their dampened enthusiasm says it all. 

As they recheck Rohan's notes, they explain the passkey's design. The compass, tuned to the shifting unpredictability of the Nexus, should bring you right to the Black Garden's door. 

There, the Seed of Silver Wings, refractive with the Garden's fluctuating DNA, should allow you to enter as if you belong.

Nimbus presses their Cloud Strider core. A whirl of nanites fly out, welding the components together. 

As they work, Nimbus points out a name in Rohan's notes: the Conceptual Mind.

This is the architect Rohan saw building the Black Heart 10 years ago. It's also your best chance at unlocking the Veil, following the Witness, and bringing a worthy end to Rohan's unfinished business.

They hand over the finished passkey and wish you good luck.

Head to In.Gress to launch the "What Remains" mission.

Nimbus beams as you approach, clapping you on the shoulder. "Well, well, well! If it isn't the hero of the hour!" 

Not even the remaining threats to the city can dim their enthusiasm, it seems. Their smile turns wry as they look out over Neomuna.

"Job's not done yet. But it's easier to shoulder the burden with a helping hand. And I'm glad it's yours."

You have completed the Legendary campaign. Please select your reward.
As a reward for completing the Legendary campaign, you have received Strand Meditations to help in the battles to come.

Nimbus claps you on the back in greeting. After everything that's happened, you are a true ally of Neomuna and welcome in the city anytime.

"We may not be the hottest tourist spot in the system," they quip, looking out at the smoldering skyline, "but we'll take all the help we can get."

There's an ironic twist to the Cloud Strider's mouth, but it can't cover up the worry in their eyes. "Osiris filled me in on everything else that's happened. The Witness created some kind of portal in your Traveler and went through it, right? If it's rejecting all probes… then forget about getting people through it."

"I can't claim we've got the answers, but we're all in this together, right? Humanity's gotta help each other, Neptune or Earth. Neomuna's role in this war isn't over by a long shot. While everyone figures out what's next, could use your help holding the line here. The less gets by us, the less comes at you later.  And when we do know what's next, Neomuna's got your back. It's our galaxy too."

"Hey, Guardian. Is that a Neomun-Pie that I spy?!" Nimbus asks as you hand them a delicious Neomun-Pie.

"Did you… bake this yourself? REALLY?! That's amazing! Never had a 'home cooked' Neomun-Pie before though. I bet it's better than the ones in the vending receptacles."

As Nimbus munches on the Neomun-Pie you hear a muffled, "Thank you, Guardian, you rock! Happy Dawning!"

You power-cycled the CloudArk—the tech built off the Veil that keeps all Neomuni citizens linked in their virtual infrastructure. With the CloudArk back online, they'll be able to contribute more to resisting Calus's assault on their city. Your recent success with Strand has Osiris and Nimbus thinking it's worth exploring further, as another potential advantage over Calus. You're still not ready for a head-on assault but, maybe with Strand, you can be. 

After a pleasant chat with Osiris, Nimbus was reminded of a place that you and the Old Bird might find useful for mastering Strand. Before they hand you the coordinates, they take a moment to tell you just how much you amaze them. It took Rohan a while to give Nimbus their first compliment on the job, and they made a promise that they'd do it differently when they took over. The old man might think compliments go to your head, but Nimbus sees nothing but good in appreciating people when they deserve it.

Nimbus recommends you check in with Rohan and Osiris at the Hall of Heroes before moving on to mission "On The Verge."

Nimbus introduces themself as the "Rookie Cloud Strider" in Neomuna. Nimbus, their superior, Rohan, and the long line of Cloud Striders who came before them have been keeping the city and its citizens safe for a long time sans-Guardians. Nimbus isn't sure what Guardians can bring to the table now, but it seems Neomuna and the Vanguard have similar enemies. It can't hurt to work together, right?

Complete the mission "Under Siege" in Neomuna.

All Nimbus had to hear was "Strand weapon" for them to hop on board with your project. "What a great idea! Why didn't we think of this sooner?" they practically shout in enthusiasm. 

They switch to brainstorming mode. "Hm. A weapon that harnesses the Veil's energy… can't be made outta your everyday stuff. At the very least, you'll need the same grade materials as the Veil Containment." 

The Cloud Strider perks up. "Actually, you could just retrofit some of the Irkalla Institute's old equipment. I bet their atmospheric spectrometers are chock full of Strand energy!"

Search Veil Containment for an atmospheric Veil spectrometer.

Nimbus is bummed about the outcome of the last mission—they were really rooting for you. They sympathize by recounting Rohan's little catchphrase for such an occasion: "Headlong and empty-handed," explaining that it's okay to stop trying to do it all yourself; we're in this together. We'll fix this. 

Whatever the Witness wants from the Veil clearly involves using the Radial Mast to create some sort of… link? So the threat remains high. But right now, the CloudArk—Neomuna's virtual infrastructure built on the Veil's power—needs our help. "I'm sure you've seen the virtual citizens milling about the city. You see… nah, you know what, I'll explain details on the way. Point is, to protect the Veil, we need to protect the CloudArk." Your direct assault on Calus failed. Time to try a different approach.

Nimbus recommends you check in with Rohan and Osiris at the Hall of Heroes before moving on to mission "Breakneck."

Nimbus congratulates you on the progress you've made with Strand. They council on your next steps, saying that now is probably the best time for you and Osiris to try to master the element. Nimbus also thinks Rohan would agree.

As a sign of the trust you have built together, Nimbus refers to themself with their true name: Cloud Strider Dara Danu. They thought you should know.

Complete the mission "Headlong" in Neomuna.

"Bluejay, huh? That's a heck of a story." Nimbus grins. "Jain had serious problems with authority. Makes me look like an Academy drill instructor by comparison. Big brain, though, and an even bigger heart. Once he learned to actually listen to others, he went from public enemy to public hero. Eventually became a Cloud Strider."

"The Cloud Striders maintain the original sim space he built way back when. It's technically in the VexNet, so we use it like a listening post. Problem is, with everything going on, it's full of Vex. Locked with a quadrinomial encryption sequence too. Nasty stuff. You'd need a Polymorphic Engine to crack it. And a ton of their Shellcode samples."

They pat you on the shoulder. "This is the part where I tell you to stay away. 'It's too dangerous.' But neither of us would believe it coming from me."

Destroy Vex and gather their Shellcode Fragments to continue bonding with this legacy.

Nimbus admits to leaving the induction ceremony early; it doesn't feel right when Neomuna is still overrun and the Witness is at large. 

If you ask them, a better way to honor Rohan's legacy would be to finish his unfinished business and find the Vex's copycat Veil.

Apparently, early in his training, Rohan stumbled on the Vex building what he believed was a copy of the Veil. Convinced this was a threat, he spent the rest of his career trying to retrace his steps through the Nexus. Nimbus believes Rohan succeeded right before the Shadow Legion's invasion. 

They ask for your help finding Rohan's notes, hidden all around the city in encrypted data packets. To recover the data, you will need cipher qubits, which can be collected from the Vex.

Defeat Vex in Neomuna to collect qubits and recover Rohan's data packets.

Nimbus admits they weren't as settled with Rohan's death as they thought they were. Cloud Striders are trained to accept death as part of the flow. To Nimbus, that meant pushing through the pain, trying to outrun their grief. 

Seeing Rohan's gun in the Black Garden forced them to stop and realize just how much they missed him. 

Nimbus thanks you for seeing the mission through. With the Conceptual Mind's memory core, the odds of unlocking the Veil and following the Witness have shot up. 

Nimbus promises to deliver the memory core so Osiris and Neomuna's researchers can start decrypting it. 

There's just one stop Nimbus has to make first.

Go to the Hall of Heroes to honor those who cut their years short for the sake of humanity.

Calus is gone.

With an uncharacteristically heavy voice, Nimbus confides they aren't sure what victory looks like going forward, but they're not going to let that undercut the relief that their home and their people are safe.

It feels weird to not be "the rookie" anymore, they tell you; Rohan left big shoes to fill. Nimbus's voice takes a hopeful upturn: they'll get there someday.

They invite you to Rohan's induction ceremony into the Hall of Heroes, telling you Rohan would be honored if you attended.

While Nimbus supports going on the offense, they caution you not to forget the ordinary people caught in the crossfire.

The people of Neomuna are skeptical of Earth's Warlords, and they're caught between dual assaults from the Shadow Legion and Vex. Nimbus has some ideas for how you can tackle both problems at once.

Complete tasks to bolster the city's defenses and improve relations between Earth and Neomuna.

Nimbus greets you with their usual enthusiasm. "Guardian! Listen, Osiris just got in touch. He says his data crawler uncovered all kinds of weird stuff."

Their smile becomes a little self-deprecating. "You're better at understanding ancient history and… what did the old bird call it? Paracausal studies? Something like that. The point is, I think you'll get more out of Osiris's data crawler than I will."

"Head back down there and take a look. And let me know if you find anything interesting."

With Rohan gone, the weight of protecting Neomuna falls heaviest on Nimbus's shoulders. Their greeting lacks its usual cheer, but they rally enough to attempt a smile.

"Me? Aw, don't worry, I've got it all handled! But between you and me, the citizens could really use some hope right now. People will feel better knowing our allies have our backs."

"Hey, Guardian! Thanks for coming down."

"We've had some weird Vex activity going on across the city in the last couple weeks. When I sent the data to Osiris, he got all excited about it." Nimbus smirks. "You know how he gets."

Nimbus rolls their shoulders, ready for action. "Osiris thinks whatever the Vex are after has to do with the Veil, and he wants you to look into it; collect some data, see what they've been digging into." Nimbus sighs.

"Where one Kell sees detritus, another finds opportunity. And there is so much detritus borne from the territory war you've started." His shoulders shake as he chuckles. "Let's see what my scavengers have found you. As long as this conflict goes on, there's profit to be made." 

He taps his fingers eagerly as you open his gift.

Spider leans back and guffaws into the air. "You enraged all three major syndicates in a single infiltration of the Lawless Frontier," he spits gleefully. "Well done, renegade. Your reward: a few ontological materials Drifter's Ghost will need. Kitbash her with these, and she'll be good as new." He reaches out, four paws full of glittering, paracausal metals.

Spider hunches towards you eagerly. "You're in luck. The Pikers have agreed to a deal for a Splicer Shank under the condition that you go and help them with a little side project first."

"Go make your introduction with Riliks and see how you might be of service. They don't give their trust away lightly, but when Riliks respects you and your code? Perhaps we can manipulate them." Spider snickers lightly to himself.

"War beckons, my renegade!" Spider booms. "War among the Syndicates for power, prestige, territory! And above all, profit!"

He leans forward, looming over you from his raised seat. "You did this, you know. With the Imperium neutralized, a power vacuum has opened on the Lawless Frontier. Everything is up for grabs, and that includes your allyship.

"The Syndicates and their quartermasters have all come to me—on bended knee, mind you—to ask for your assistance."

Spider winks his glowing eyes. "Give them a moment of your time, will you? And remember that out here, today's ally can always be tomorrow's rival. Follow the Glimmer, Guardian. Follow the Glimmer."

Spider chortles low and gleefully as you approach. "I've always liked Drifter's Ghost," he says. "She's the best thing about him! If she's finally looking to get her voice back, I'd be glad to help. For a small favor." He gestures towards the dark corners of the den. "My transport crews have failed me. I sent them into the Lawless Frontier to bring back hard-won contraband. If you'll venture out there, find my crew, and more importantly, my contraband—I'll make sure you obtain the Ghost parts you still need."

Spider leans forward eagerly as you approach. "Tharsis has been overrun by delinquency," he roars, huffing the air. "Feels more like home than Variisis Core ever did. Hold on to your Glimmer; it's not the anchor coinage of Mars. You'll need Credits to entice the Tharsis Syndicates and craft specialists. And I'd be happy to part you from your Credits in exchange for frontier tech, purchased directly from yours truly. Go on. You deserve a shopping spree now that you're free of your Vanguard bonds. When you're done, your old pal Drifter has news from the Pikers."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Mechanic Deoriks waves you over, a stack of datapads heaped precariously in the crook of one elbow.

"Good news, latest shipment's just in. Riliks told me to reserve a portion of it for you in thanks for your efforts last week. Spider's holding onto it for you."

She clacks her mandibles. "Don't love Spider getting his greasy hands on our stuff, but Riliks says we gotta pick our battles sometimes. And in this case, victory is meditating on the lovely warm memory of Spider's barge exploding."

Deoriks flags you down with a wave of a datapad.

"You're the Guardian Vixis has been talking to? Well, I guess if you're helping him out, you're all right for a Lightbearer," she says.

"You ever ride a Pike? A Falcon's like that, but more. I can list every component we use in 'em and where we get 'em, but I don't want to keep you when you've got Imperium goons to squash.

"Remember—if you're not scared you're about to crash, you're not going fast enough."

The Pikers' quartermaster Deoriks beckons you over with a confiding air.

"You know us, Guardian. Do you want the frontier run by a military force with Imperium ties? Or a bunch of soup that likes to gamble? Pikers are the only answer."

She leans in. "Listen, Riliks is a weird one, but they've got vision. I've never regretted joining up. I'll take this gang over any House you could name. 

"We've got the best tech, the best perks, and—let's be honest here—the best company. Ride with the Pikers, Guardian. You won't regret it."
Deposit Dark Matter Ingots at the Pikers War Chest to earn Reputation with this Syndicate. Earn Renegade Abilities, Praxic Blade modifications, gear, and currency.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
The air around the Pouka Pond thrums with extra energy upon your return. Even the poukas are trilling with excitement, as they flit across the surface of the water like skipping stones.

In the midst of this inspired atmosphere, it takes almost no time for you to combine the retuned spectrometer with the found Neomuni nanites. 

Metallic bits and green threads whirl as they knit together a mighty fine Strand weapon.

You pick up the gun—it feels just right—then stow it along with the rest of your arms.

You can now wield Strand in all respects.

Osiris has left a note behind for you. It reads:

Guardian, 

I do not know where our research into the Veil will bring us. The work done by Chioma Esi and Maya Sundaresh is undoubtedly critical to our understanding of not only the Veil but also its greater purpose in the Witness's agenda. We have only begun to scratch the surface. I wish there were more time.

Regardless, even the beginning of our work has borne fruit in further understanding Strand through its source of origin within the Veil. The more we understand of one, the more we understand of the other. In that, I believe, there is hope.

In the meantime, I believe there are other obligations that demand your attention. I will let you know of any future developments.

Warmest Regards,
Osiris

At the Pouka Pond, you hold the Veil spectrometer. It pulses with Strand energy, but something about it feels off. The vibrations are uneven, out of sync with what's around you.  

Perhaps the Shadow Legion tampered with it. Or perhaps you simply need to reset its energetic signature. 

Osiris's training program helped you get into the rhythm of using Strand before. A speedy run-through should be enough to align the spectrometer's energy with your unique combat tempo. 

Complete Osiris's training program in Radiosonde to retune the spectrometer's Strand vibrations.

Now that you've mastered the power of Strand, the time has come to get creative with it. Meditating at the Pouka Pond sparks an exciting notion. How might you incorporate Strand energy into your weapons? 

The Cloud Striders have developed some interesting weapons systems over the years. Perhaps Nimbus could help you out with their nanites. At the very least, they'll be eager to brainstorm on a cool new gun.

Visit Nimbus in Striders' Gate to discuss incorporating Strand into a weapon.

The pond shimmers as pouka weave in and out of it, navigating water and air easily as though there were no difference between the two. Sparkling droplets scatter from their fins. In the moment, it is easy to see again how all things are connected, how one strand plucked here resonates at a great distance with all of the others.

There is a new power here, between the stillness and the motion. Reach for it, and it is yours.

A new grenade is available for purchase from the Pouka Pond.

You harnessed the power of Strand and defeated Calus. But the journey is far from over…

Strand Meditations allow you to unlock the full potential of Strand and become a true master. Use them to purchase new Strand Aspects, Fragments, and grenades.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
Lodi turns to you urgently as you approach. "The Nine wax and wane, like a tide. Something about my relationship to them has changed. Will. Is changing. Heh, sorry! I'm… I'm…" He gasps as the Nine overwhelm him with a vision.

"I'm ten miles outside of Allen, South Dakota. 1960. I eat iodine tablets like popcorn and walk on the deck of a ship that appeared… in the ravine." He snorts, disoriented.

"I'm weightless, like… a coin in midair; a beach after an earthquake, before the tsunami. I—Don't worry, I'm here. I'm with you." He was speaking to you, but then he laughs, suddenly, his context shifting again.

"I'm in Madison, Wisconsin. It's 1929. I think that biplane is the most beautiful thing I've ever seen. I want to be up there." He blinks, and it seems like he finally sees you for a moment.

"The Nine are going to come back, and I'll stop them. They stretched me across time and didn't think I'd learn to use it for myself. Hold infinity in the palm of your hand and eternity in an hour. See?"

"It's 1962… and I'm in Lodi, Wisconsin. I feed ducks on the pond downtown. I drove there. My hands hurt from the cold. Ben's sitting next to me…"

He breathes in shakily, shifting his weight again. "It's years from now. You've learned enough Welsh to do more than just curse. Your accent still needs work."

He looks directly at you, now. "I'm not going anywhere. I'll call you sometime, Guardian."

Lodi greets you with warmth and a little twirl as you admire his scarf, "Hey, what do you think of the new look? Took some doing to find a local tailor who did more than robes, but I finally feel dressed for the job." 
 
The two of you share a silent, thoughtful moment. Weapon and Emissary, connected by a shared fate. But, equally, connected by friendship.

He sobers a little as he continues, "As kind as everyone has been, I can tell the Prophecy is still on their minds. And with good reason. The Outer Nine at work, undermining our reality. They're dead set on escaping Sol, no matter the cost. And if they degrade the integrity of our spacetime enough, they could do it."
 
Lodi frowns at you, deep sympathy in his gaze. "I hate to put yet another crisis on your plate, but these Nine-based distortions are manifesting across Sol causing all kinds of problem. The Vanguard is calling this an all-hands-on-deck situation. Good luck out there."

interactions.flavorLineOne:
As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, Rojin's words form in your mind. 

"This is all that is needed to align with the final strangelet."

There is a brief pause as calculations are run and ciphers are drafted. The Altar hums along.

"The Gorge can be accessed. Be wary, Anomaly-Blessed. The automatons that attacked Kepler have made the Gorge their home. Orin, saint of the Anomaly, has already departed to face them. Together, you will prevail."

The Altar of Relativity hums as you approach, and an armament for the Weapon materializes.

Collect your reward for completing all missions on Legendary difficulty.

The Altar of Relativity appears to be a relic of a bygone era—a jump drive converted from pre-Golden Age technology. It's been damaged and repaired with components that are obviously straining to contain the forces surging inside. Ghost remarks, "Singularity stabilizers likely aren't an off-the-shelf item."

The Aionians have been extremely clever and resourceful in assembling this complex device, despite their relative lack of resources. Still, the altar is definitely unstable. Strangelet capsules appear to be the only method of effectively stabilizing the altar, and by extension, the singularity.

As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, Rojin's words form in your mind. 

"Anomaly-Blessed, your field work is efficient and thorough. We are fortunate to have found favor with you. With the return of another strangelet, we are able to cull bad data from our hypotheses. We've narrowed your next destination to the Outer Steppes. We are locking the Altar to that strangelet capsule now." 

"Go in certainty."

As you approach the Altar you feel a strange kind of hum. It is not audible, but you can feel it both physically and paracausually within you.
There is also something else there, a new…feeling? It's not anything you've experienced before. It's some kind of resonance beyond the physical and paracausal.
You feel satiated, and yet there is a sense that there is much more to whet your appetite on this planetoid… and elsewhere.
It seems that you've taken your first step into a larger, stranger world.

The language of the interface is indecipherable, but the altar appears to be unpowered. It cannot process a strangelet capsule integration.

Ghost is tracing power transfers around the altar site. The source appears to be dark matter conduits, most likely kept away from the Aionian security zone for safety.

Ghost believes it's possible to restore power.

As you access the interface, it melds with Rosetta, speaking words from an Aionian into your inner voice. 

"Anomaly-Blessed. I am Rojin, the Altar's technician, and the one honored to deliver what help we can. We offer, in awe, our findings to aid you. Should you see fit, your impressive drone will receive actionable data to locate strangelet capsules, and use the Altar's relativistic connection with them as a cipher to pass into the cordoned regions of Kepler. With our current integrations and research, you will gain access to the Central Academy and the Exile's Accord."

There is a brief pause as Ghost accepts the data transmission.

"Most gracious, Anomaly-blessed. Transfer commencing."

"We shall continue our research into the other stolen strangelets. With further integrations, the remaining capsules will increase synchronicity with the Altar and allow us to impose a shifted perspective that ignores the cordons by our observation of the strangelet beyond them. It is a delicate alignment, but our efforts can only improve through iteration."
Track your Fabled exploration progress and strangelet capsule collection.
Collect strangelet capsules in World Tier: Mythic and integrate them at the Altar of Relativity.

interactions.flavorLineOne:
"Aghol. Totality Armorer. And you're the Lightbearer who's raised such a ruckus around the place."

The Armorer eyes you up and down. "Well, I don't mind a bit of a ruckus myself. There are plenty of abandoned drop pods scattered across Sol's old battlefields. Easy enough to recover and repurpose as artillery."

"Even Guardians know, nothing outside the pod survives contact with the pod." Aghol laughs loudly, and hands you a beacon.

Armorer Aghol clears his throat. "Got some more legalese for you, Lightbearer. You ready?"

"'The Totality Division is grateful for your continued support. The rewards promised you are being held in escrow by Spider. If you have any issues with the delivery, we request that you take it up with him. With regards from Enforcer Rao."

"Glad I don't have to write that stuff myself," Aghol says. "But we mean it."

Aghol scratches his chin. "Looking for a Syndicate to ally with? I won't say we couldn't use you, Guardian. And you couldn't do better than the Totality Division.

"One thing about the Division is, Rao doesn't brook any nonsense. We won't mess with your Glimmer. We share resources accordingly. What am I gonna do with a Praxic Blade, cut my hand off? Any mods come in, they're earmarked for you—if you earn 'em."

"I'll see you back here soon, yeah?"
Deposit Dark Matter Ingots at the Totality Division War Chest to earn Reputation with this Syndicate. Earn Renegade Abilities, Praxic Blade modifications, gear, and currency.
